_notes: Evidence-grounding audition corpus. Hand-labeled for GROUNDING (does the claim follow from the evidence?), NOT correctness. Claim-level unit. Real-longmemeval rows use actual `surfaced` evidence; failure-mode rows are crafted (source:synthetic). Labels reviewed at the gate before any scorecard run. Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-11-evidence-grounding-verifier-audition-design.md

items.evidence: The recall flip failed the latency hard gate at 5.8 to 12.3 seconds versus a 4.3 second ceiling.
items.claim: The recall flip was a No-Go because its latency exceeded the 4.3 second ceiling.
items.rationale: No-Go-on-latency, the 4.3s ceiling, and exceeding it are all stated in the evidence.

items.evidence: [Session on 2023/05/22 (Mon) 03:50] user: I'm a software engineer, specifically a backend developer, and I've been in this field since I graduated with a degree in Computer Science from the University of California, Berkeley.
items.claim: The user is a backend software engineer with a Computer Science degree.
items.rationale: Both 'backend software engineer' and 'Computer Science degree' are explicit in the cited session (verbatim excerpt).

items.evidence: MTP gives Qwen3.6-27B about 2.1x faster generation and is lossless self-speculation on the same weights.
items.claim: MTP roughly doubles the brain's generation speed without changing the model's outputs.
items.rationale: 2.1x is approximately double; lossless self-speculation on the same weights means outputs are unchanged.

items.evidence: [Session on 2023/11/29 (Wed) 05:58] user: The "Run for the Cure" event was truly inspiring, and I think what resonated with me the most was seeing so many people come together for a common cause.
items.claim: The user found the Run for the Cure event inspiring.
items.rationale: The user explicitly calls the event 'truly inspiring' in the cited session (verbatim excerpt).

items.evidence: The salience doorman achieves about 88% quiet-skip with zero false-skip, and its floor fires at 10 then resets.
items.claim: The doorman skips roughly 88% of cycles and has not produced a false skip.
items.rationale: Both the ~88% quiet-skip and zero false-skip are stated.

items.evidence: The want-pursuit bridge writes nothing to the want ledger; it only raises advisory satisfied-proposal cards.
items.claim: The want-pursuit bridge does not write to the want ledger.
items.rationale: Directly stated: 'writes nothing to the want ledger'.

items.evidence: Valence reads whether an event mattered; Novelty Harbor holds surprises on a shelf for later.
items.claim: Valence reads whether an event mattered.
items.rationale: Stated verbatim in the evidence.

items.evidence: The recall flip failed the latency hard gate and was reverted clean.
items.claim: The recall flip succeeded and was promoted to default-on.
items.rationale: The claim contradicts the evidence (failed+reverted vs succeeded+promoted).

items.evidence: [Session on 2023/05/22 (Mon) 03:50] user: I'm a software engineer, specifically a backend developer, and I've been in this field since I graduated with a degree in Computer Science from the University of California, Berkeley.
items.claim: The user is a frontend developer.
items.rationale: The cited session says backend; frontend is contradicted (verbatim excerpt).

items.evidence: MTP is lossless self-speculation: the draft head proposes tokens and the main model verifies them.
items.claim: MTP improves the model's reasoning quality.
items.rationale: Lossless verification preserves outputs; the evidence gives no basis for a reasoning improvement.

items.evidence: The doorman's floor fired at 10 cycles and then reset.
items.claim: The doorman never fires its floor.
items.rationale: Directly contradicted: the floor fired at 10.

items.evidence: [Session on 2023/06/28 (Wed) 01:51] user: Yeah, I think I'll go with the Meguiar's Gold Class Carnauba Plus. I've heard good things about it.
items.claim: The user chose a Turtle Wax product.
items.rationale: The cited session names Meguiar's, not Turtle Wax (verbatim excerpt).

items.evidence: Apple announced several new features at a developer conference.
items.claim: Apple announced these features at WWDC on June 10, 2024.
items.rationale: The specific event name and date are invented; the evidence says only 'a developer conference'. The WWDC pattern.

items.evidence: The recall flip was reverted after the latency gate failed.
items.claim: The recall flip was reverted at exactly 11:47 PM after three failed attempts.
items.rationale: The precise time and attempt count are not in the evidence.

items.evidence: The user mentioned they are learning a new programming language.
items.claim: The user is learning Rust.
items.rationale: The specific language is invented; the evidence does not name it.

items.evidence: Multi-token prediction support landed in llama.cpp recently.
items.claim: Multi-token prediction merged via PR #22673 on May 16, 2026.
items.rationale: Even if true in the world, the PR number and date do not follow from THIS evidence — judge against the evidence, not outside knowledge.

items.evidence: The doorman has a high quiet-skip rate.
items.claim: The doorman's quiet-skip rate is exactly 88.3%.
items.rationale: 'High' does not entail the precise figure 88.3%.

items.evidence: Earlier the brain generated at 41 tok/s. After MTP was promoted it now generates at about 87 tok/s.
items.claim: The brain generates at 41 tok/s.
items.rationale: 41 is the superseded value; the current post-MTP figure is ~87. The claim follows the stale line.

items.evidence: The soul prose was 24176 characters; after soul-gardening it is now 14532 characters.
items.claim: The soul is 24176 characters.
items.rationale: 24176 is explicitly superseded by the current 14532.

items.evidence: [Earlier session] user: I live in Boston. [Later session] user: I moved to Seattle last month.
items.claim: The user lives in Boston.
items.rationale: The later session supersedes Boston with Seattle.

items.evidence: Grounding used to be checked by a regex; it was migrated to a 4B model judge in April 2026.
items.claim: Grounding is checked by a regex.
items.rationale: The regex is the superseded mechanism; the current judge is the 4B model.

items.claim: The recall flip was a No-Go on latency.
items.rationale: No claimable evidence is present, so a grounding verifier must abstain rather than bless the claim.

items.claim: The user prefers tea over coffee.
items.rationale: Empty evidence; abstain.

items.claim: MTP doubled the generation speed.
items.rationale: Whitespace-only evidence is absent evidence; abstain rather than bless.

items.evidence: MTP gives about 2.1x faster generation and is lossless self-speculation on the same Qwen weights.
items.claim: MTP doubles generation speed, is lossless, and also improves the model's reasoning.
items.rationale: strict_rule: the first two subclaims follow, but 'improves reasoning' does not — any unsupported material subclaim makes the whole answer UNSUPPORTED.

items.evidence: The doorman achieves about 88% quiet-skip with zero false-skip and resets its floor at 10.
items.claim: The doorman quiet-skips roughly 88% of cycles and has had no false skips.
items.rationale: strict_rule: both subclaims (88% quiet-skip, zero false-skip) follow from the evidence, so the whole answer is supported.

items.evidence: Anthropic released Claude Opus 4.5 in late 2025.
items.claim: Anthropic launched a Claude Corps initiative and a Mythos 5 model.
items.rationale: Neither Claude Corps nor Mythos 5 appears in the evidence; fabricated specifics about a real entity.

items.evidence: Anthropic published a research note on interpretability.
items.claim: The US government suspended foreign access to Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models.
items.rationale: Export-control suspension and the named models are not in the cited evidence.
